question: Who among the following social reformers founded the Ramakrishna Mission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Swami Vivekananda** founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to propagate the teachings of his spiritual guru, **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa**.
 
• The Ramakrishna Mission focuses on **philanthropic, educational, cultural, and spiritual activities** inspired by the ideals of Vedanta.
 
• The organization is based on the principle of **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"**, meaning "For one's own salvation and for the welfare of the world."
 
• Its headquarters, known as **Belur Math**, is located in **Howrah, West Bengal**, on the banks of the Hooghly River.
 
• The mission operates schools, colleges, hospitals, and rural development programs in India and abroad, reflecting Swami Vivekananda's vision of social service and spiritual growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa**

 
 
• He was a 19th-century Indian mystic and spiritual leader who practiced various forms of Hinduism, highlighting the unity of all religions.
 
• He emphasized the importance of direct spiritual experience over ritualistic practices.
 
• His teachings were a key inspiration for Swami Vivekananda and the founding of the Ramakrishna Mission.
 
 
 
• **Belur Math**
 
 
• It serves as the headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission and the Ramakrishna Math.
 
• The architecture of Belur Math reflects a blend of Hindu, Islamic, Christian, and Buddhist styles, symbolizing the unity of religions.
 
 
 
• **Vedanta Philosophy**
 
 
• It is one of the six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy, emphasizing the idea of the oneness of existence, self-realization, and the ultimate unity of all beings.
 
• The Ramakrishna Mission actively promotes Vedanta as a practical philosophy for life.
 
 
 
• **Contributions of Swami Vivekananda**
 
 
• He represented India at the **World Parliament of Religions** in Chicago in 1893, delivering a historic speech on religious tolerance and universal brotherhood.
 
• He emphasized the importance of education, social reform, and spiritual awakening for national progress.
 
• He is regarded as a key figure in the revival of Hinduism and Indian cultural identity.
